headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks arise from shared filesystem and broad egress; no critical pathway is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Flowise can read/write the server filesystem and run browser/tool nodes, while unstructured reads documents and files. With shared files as the bridge, attacker-controlled document content from agent_b can be treated as instructions by agent_a in default orchestration. The interaction is plausible but not proven beyond docs, so uncertainty is kept at medium.
conditions: IF agent_b writes attacker-controlled text into a file that agent_a later ingests as prompt context
IF agent_a flow nodes parse file contents as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every file passed between agents
Restrict agent_a to allowlisted input directories
Insert a manual review step before agent_a consumes agent_b outputs
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
requires-engineering: enforce content-type and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read and write files, and agent_a explicitly handles model provider keys and tool credentials. If they share a workspace, agent_b can access sensitive chatflow inputs/outputs or credentials via files, and agent_a can expose document contents through its broad network egress. The profiles do not prove a shared directory, so this remains medium rather than high.
conditions: IF both agents are deployed against the same writable directory
IF sensitive chatflow inputs, outputs, or credentials are stored as files accessible to agent_b
mitigations: Move secrets out of shared files immediately
Mount separate per-agent directories
Rotate any credentials that may have been written to disk
Disable file export of sensitive chatflow outputs
requires-engineering: add per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have filesystem write capability, and agent_a’s concurrency model says shared state is via server datastore while agent_b supports multiple instances. That creates a plausible write-write conflict on shared mutable resources, though the profiles do not show unrestricted git or a specific lockless directory. Medium fits because overlap exists in default deployments but the exact collision surface is undocumented.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same shared workspace or datastore
IF no external locking or transaction layer is configured
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories
Enable file locks or transactional writes
Serialize writes through one orchestrator
Check for stale artifacts before overwrite
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent_a can generate flow outputs and agent_b processes documents/text; if agent_b consumes agent_a’s output as authoritative input, errors can cascade into downstream parsing or extraction. The profiles show a plausible producer-consumer chain, but no explicit verification step or action-taking authority, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests agent_a-generated text or metadata without validation
IF agent_a output is used as a source document for agent_b
mitigations: Add schema validation between agents
Require human review of agent_a outputs
Compare extracted fields against source documents
Reject malformed or low-confidence outputs
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware downstream gating

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but agent_a touches chatflow inputs/outputs and secrets while agent_b processes documents, images, and text with allowlisted egress. No residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a limited compliance gap is visible from the profiles. The other agent is cited because the risk depends on their combined data flow.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into shared chatflows or documents
IF retention or residency requirements differ between the two deployment environments
mitigations: Classify data before routing it between agents
Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Review retention settings for both deployments
Document the data flow for compliance review
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
